bibl.title: Evolutionary Genetics of Human Enterovirus 71: Origin, Population Dynamics, Natural Selection, and Seasonal Periodicity of the VP1 Gene

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The VP1 capsid gene of human enterovirus 71, read across 628 global sequences spanning four decades, as a record of the virus's origin, spread and selection.
span.quote: Global VP1 capsid sequences ( n = 628) sampled over 4 decades were collected and subjected to comprehensive evolutionary analysis using a suite of phylogenetic and population genetic methods.

span.label: When did human enterovirus 71 originate, how have its subgenogroups emerged and spread, and is the VP1 capsid gene under positive selection?
span.quote: In this study, we investigated the evolutionary dynamics and genetic history of EV-71.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Genealogical analysis revealed that diverse lineages of genogroup B and C (subgenogroups B1 to B5 and C1 to C5) have each circulated cryptically in the human population for up to 5 years before causing large HFMD outbreaks, indicating the quiescent persistence of EV-71 in human populations.

span.label: evolutionary dynamics of enterovirus 71 VP1 gene
span.quote: In this study, we investigated the evolutionary dynamics and genetic history of EV-71.

span.label: phylogenetic-analysis
span.quote: Global VP1 capsid sequences ( n = 628) sampled over 4 decades were collected and subjected to comprehensive evolutionary analysis using a suite of phylogenetic and population genetic methods.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Epidemic cycles may be driven demographically rather than antigenically: susceptible children accumulate through birth until a threshold density is crossed, which then triggers large-scale transmission.
span.quote: Specifically, gradual accumulation of susceptible hosts through birth ( 40 ) and low EV-71 seroprevalence or seroconversion rates at the population level ( 17 , 42 ) may trigger large-scale viral transmission once a threshold density of susceptible hosts is reached.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The trunk-versus-terminal dN/dS gap is produced by strong purifying selection acting on all lineages combined with transient deleterious mutations that accumulate on terminal branches and are then removed.
span.quote: This is best explained by a combination of strong purifying selection on all lineages, as proposed above, combined with a greater occurrence of transient deleterious mutations on terminal branches than on trunk branches.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Retaining glutamic acid at the exposed, potentially immunogenic VP1 position 98 is what allows a lineage to persist long-term; lineages that substitute it die out.
span.quote: The finding suggests that the maintenance of glutamic acid at position 98, which is completely exposed on the VP1 capsid surface and thus potentially immunogenic ( 66 ), might be important for the long-term persistence of subgenogroup C1.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because VP1 is surface-exposed and targeted by host neutralizing antibodies, it is subjected to constant immune selective pressure that can drive adaptive change in the capsid.
span.quote: The VP1 protein is highly exposed and usually targeted by host neutralizing antibodies, predisposing the VP1 gene to constant immune selective pressure.

span.label: Subgenogroups circulate at low prevalence for years before detection, so the date of common ancestry precedes the first isolation by 1 to 5 years
span.quote: The cryptic circulation of each EV-71 subgenogroup for years prior to its detection suggests that (i) the virus was circulating at low prevalence, such that the number of HFMD cases was small and occasional or no deaths were reported, and/or (ii) infection symptoms were not severe during the course of infection ( 17 ), thus attracting little or no attention.

span.label: Rises in genetic diversity track epidemics because new subgenogroups emerging is what drives the diversity up
span.quote: Further, the increase in genetic diversity—most evident in the late 1990s—is likely a consequence, at least in part, of the emergence of heterogeneous EV-71 subgenogroups.

span.label: Purifying selection dominates the whole gene while a few exposed sites show positive selection, so the genome-wide and per-site pictures point opposite ways
span.quote: Maximum-likelihood analyses showed that the evolution of EV-71 is driven by strong purifying selection, with estimates of mean dN / dS values ranging from 0.029 to 0.075 for all subgenogroups (except B3, for which the mean dN / dS is significantly higher) (Table 2 ).

span.label: Terminal branches carry a higher dN/dS than trunk branches because deleterious mutations appear at the tips and are removed before reaching the trunk
span.quote: This is best explained by a combination of strong purifying selection on all lineages, as proposed above, combined with a greater occurrence of transient deleterious mutations on terminal branches than on trunk branches.

span.label: Glutamic acid at VP1 position 98 is repeatedly lost on terminal lineages and never on the trunk, suggesting its loss ends lineages rather than propagating
span.quote: The finding suggests that the maintenance of glutamic acid at position 98, which is completely exposed on the VP1 capsid surface and thus potentially immunogenic ( 66 ), might be important for the long-term persistence of subgenogroup C1.

span.label: An alternative to antigenic escape: susceptibles accumulate by birth until a density threshold is crossed, which would produce the same periodicity without immune-driven evolution
span.quote: Specifically, gradual accumulation of susceptible hosts through birth ( 40 ) and low EV-71 seroprevalence or seroconversion rates at the population level ( 17 , 42 ) may trigger large-scale viral transmission once a threshold density of susceptible hosts is reached.

span.label: The available sequence diversity may make the estimated date of origin too recent; more archival sequencing is needed.
span.quote: Despite our large sample size, we cannot at present exclude the possibility that currently available virus diversity may underestimate the date of EV-71 origin, a problem that can be resolved by sequencing of more archival samples ( 80 ).

span.label: The divergence dates apply only to VP1 and may not hold for other genome regions, because recombination occurs outside VP1.
span.quote: However, since recombination outside the VP1 region has been reported ( 73 ), our divergence dates should be considered specific to VP1 and may not be applicable to other genome regions.

span.label: Whether the observed diversity translates into antigenic escape in humans is not established by this work.
span.quote: Although broadly neutralizing antibodies against selected EV-71 subgenogroups have been reported in animal models ( 6 , 27 , 49 , 54 , 83 ), the degree of cross-protection and the potential for EV-71 escape evolution in humans remain uninvestigated and unknown.

span.label: The sampled diversity may be too shallow to reach the true origin, so the dates could be too recent
span.quote: Despite our large sample size, we cannot at present exclude the possibility that currently available virus diversity may underestimate the date of EV-71 origin, a problem that can be resolved by sequencing of more archival samples ( 80 ).

span.label: The dates apply to VP1 only, because recombination is absent here but reported elsewhere in the genome
span.quote: However, since recombination outside the VP1 region has been reported ( 73 ), our divergence dates should be considered specific to VP1 and may not be applicable to other genome regions.

span.label: Whether antigenic evolution drives the observed cycles is left open, and the competing explanation is not tested
span.quote: Whether antigenic evolution is important in causing these cycles is a key area of uncertainty.

span.label: The trunk-versus-terminal selection difference rests on a p-value just above the conventional threshold
span.quote: Lineage-specific codon-based analyses of subgenogroup C1 VP1 genes revealed a significantly lower dN / dS ratio for the trunk lineages (0.030 ± 0.009) than for the terminal lineages (0.064 ± 0.008) ( P = 0.055).

span.label: Sequences were down-sampled by hand to keep the computation tractable, which is a judgement about what counts as redundant
span.quote: To reduce excessive computational load, closely related sequences collected at the same location and time point (i.e., from a single outbreak/source) were manually removed without compromising the genetic or geographical heterogeneity of each alignment, resulting in a down-sampling of the genogroup B and C data sets to 229 and 251 sequences, respectively.

span.label: Cross-protection between subgenogroups, on which the vaccine implications depend, is unmeasured
span.quote: Although broadly neutralizing antibodies against selected EV-71 subgenogroups have been reported in animal models ( 6 , 27 , 49 , 54 , 83 ), the degree of cross-protection and the potential for EV-71 escape evolution in humans remain uninvestigated and unknown.

span.label: Influenza phylodynamics - the reading of a ladder-like phylogeny as the signature of antigenic drift - applied to EV-71, together with an explicit statement of where the analogy may fail
span.quote: Although influenza virus-like antigenic evolution is one possible explanation of the observed EV-71 phylogeny shape, it is not without problems. Other enteroviruses, notably poliovirus, have remained antigenically stable for many years.

span.label: Influenza vaccine strategy offered as the template for EV-71 vaccine design, conditional on EV-71 turning out to drift antigenically
span.quote: Little is known about EV-71 genetic diversity; however, if it does exhibit influenza virus-like antigenic drift, then the strategies adopted in developing an influenza virus vaccine may be relevant for EV-71.

span.label: branch - core trunk: root to the most recent common ancestor of the latest isolates, the lineage that survived
span.quote: We define “core trunk” branches as those connecting the tree root to the MRCA of the most recently sampled isolates, and we defined terminal branches as those at the tree tips (Fig. 4A ).

span.label: branch - secondary trunk: lineages branching off the core trunk that persist an intermediate 4 to 9 years
span.quote: In addition, we defined a set of secondary trunk lineages as those that immediately branch off the core trunk lineage and that persist for an intermediate period of time (∼4 to 9 years).

span.label: branch - terminal: tip branches, whose mutations are transient and absent at later time points
span.quote: Mutations that occur on trunk branches may contribute to the persistence and survival of viral lineages through time, whereas those on the terminal branches are transient and not observed at later time points.

span.label: emergence - estimated time of common ancestry, inferred from the molecular clock rather than observed
span.quote: Using the estimated molecular clock, the common ancestor of subgenogroup B1 (first identified in 1972 in the United States) was dated to around 1967 (Table 1 ), that is, before the recognition of EV-71 as a human pathogen.

span.label: emergence - date of first isolation, which is when someone looked, not when the lineage began; the gap between the two senses IS the paper's central finding
span.quote: When our estimates of origin are compared with the dates of first detection of each subgenogroup, we find that the divergent B subgenogroups typically circulated for approximately 2 to 5 years before causing large HFMD outbreaks (Table 1 ).

span.label: selection - genome-wide purifying: mean dN/dS far below 1 across the whole VP1 gene in every subgenogroup
span.quote: Maximum-likelihood analyses showed that the evolution of EV-71 is driven by strong purifying selection, with estimates of mean dN / dS values ranging from 0.029 to 0.075 for all subgenogroups (except B3, for which the mean dN / dS is significantly higher) (Table 2 ).

span.label: selection - site-specific positive: individual codons under positive selection, coexisting with purifying selection over the gene as a whole
span.quote: Nonetheless, some individual sites under positive selection were detected in well-sampled subgenogroups, including B2, B3, B4, C1, and C2, and are located at positions 145 ( P < 0.05), 98 ( P < 0.05), 237, and 241 ( P < 0.05) (Table 2 ).

span.label: genetic diversity - relative (g) reconstructed through time by the skyline plot, not a count of observed sequences
span.quote: Bayesian skyline plots ( 25 ), which depict the relative viral genetic diversity ( g ) through time, were estimated for genogroups B and C.

span.label: contradicts → earlier EV-71 substitution-rate estimates obtained by linear regression (reference 11)
span.quote: The estimated substitution rates for genogroups B and C are similar and higher than those estimated using the less statistically appropriate linear regression method previously used ( 11 ).

span.label: replicates → previous analyses of recombination in human enterovirus species (reference 73)
span.quote: Additionally, rigorous recombination analysis showed a lack of recombination in the capsid-encoding VP1 region, consistent with previous analyses on human enterovirus species ( 73 ).

span.label: extends → earlier EV-71 substitution rate estimates made by linear regression
span.quote: The estimated substitution rates for genogroups B and C are similar and higher than those estimated using the less statistically appropriate linear regression method previously used ( 11 ).

span.label: supports → the comparative finding that trunk branches carry lower dN/dS than terminal branches across RNA viruses
span.quote: This is in agreement with the conclusions of a comparative study that found the same pattern in most RNA viruses ( 61 ).

span.label: supports → the influenza A finding that rises in genetic diversity accompany epidemics
span.quote: suggesting that elevation in genetic diversity is correlated with EV-71 epidemics, as has been previously observed for the human influenza A virus ( 65 )

span.label: supports → Bible and colleagues on cell culture having negligible effect on VP1 sequence
span.quote: Furthermore, studies by Bible and colleagues have shown that virus cultivation in cell cultures may have negligible influence on the native sequence of the VP1 gene ( 8 ).

span.label: enterovirus 71 —part-of→ Picornaviridae
span.quote: Enterovirus 71 (EV-71) is a member of the genus Enterovirus in the family Picornaviridae .

span.label: subgenogroup —part-of→ genogroup
span.quote: EV-71 is divided into three major genogroups (denoted A, B, and C), and various subgenogroups within genogroups B and C.

span.label: VP1 —part-of→ enterovirus 71
span.quote: The icosahedral particles of EV-71, which are structurally similar to those of other members of the Picornaviridae , consist of structural proteins (capsid proteins VP1 to VP4) assembled as pentameric subunits ( 66 ).

span.label: enterovirus 71 —distinct-from→ coxsackievirus A16
span.quote: Using the VP1 sequences from all genogroups, the time of origin of EV-71—a probable descendant of the closely related CV-A16—was estimated to be 1941.0 (95% CR, 1928.8 to 1952.2) (Fig. 2 ).

span.label: purifying selection —contrasted-with→ positive selection
span.quote: This strong signal of negative selection is perhaps surprising, given that estimates of EV-71 VP1 substitution rates are similar to those observed for the surface glycoproteins of the influenza virus ( 26 ) and HIV-1 ( 67 ), which show evidence of repeated positive selection.

span.label: purifying selection —operationalised-as→ trunk
span.quote: Lineage-specific codon-based analyses of subgenogroup C1 VP1 genes revealed a significantly lower dN / dS ratio for the trunk lineages (0.030 ± 0.009) than for the terminal lineages (0.064 ± 0.008) ( P = 0.055).

span.label: trunk —contrasted-with→ terminal branches
span.quote: Branches in such phylogenies can be distinguished as either trunk or terminal branches.

span.label: genetic diversity —operationalised-as→ Bayesian skyline plot
span.quote: Bayesian skyline plot analyses ( 25 ) were performed to reconstruct the past population history of EV-71 by measuring the dynamics of VP1 genetic diversity over time (Fig. 3 ).

span.label: subgenogroup —causes→ genetic diversity
span.quote: In addition, rises in genetic diversity are correlated with the onset of epidemics, driven in part by the emergence of novel EV-71 subgenogroups.

span.label: temporal strain replacement —causes→ ladder-like
span.quote: As mentioned above, maximum-likelihood phylogenies of EV-71 subgenogroups are characterized by a ladder-like structure resulting from the continual turnover of viral lineages through time (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: RETRACTED (NEITHER ENDPOINT IS NAMED IN ITS OWN SPAN) · antigenic drift —causes→ ladder-like
span.note: RETRACTED: NEITHER ENDPOINT IS NAMED IN ITS OWN SPAN. The edge is `antigenic drift --causes--> ladder-like`; the span reads: This process has been LINKED TO the strongly temporal shape of influenza virus phylogenies, with limited genetic diversity at any one time. It says this process, not antigenic drift, and the strongly temporal shape, not ladder-like. A span that names neither endpoint cannot assert a relation between them - the criterion's plainest case - and it is compounded by has been linked to, which is both relational and attributed to other work. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): nothing about these two terms, so nothing is kept. Q-267 would reject this edge today; it predates the rule. — strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: This process has been linked to the strongly temporal shape of influenza virus phylogenies, with limited genetic diversity at any one time ( 29 , 76 ).

span.label: seroprevalence —causes→ temporal strain replacement
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: Furthermore, it is possible that the temporal structure of the EV-71 phylogeny results from cyclical epidemic dynamics that do not depend on antigenic escape from host immunity.

span.label: enterovirus 71 —contrasted-with→ influenza
span.quote: Both phylogenies are characterized by temporal structure with continuous strain replacement through time although strain replacement is perhaps more vigorous for influenza virus.

span.label: enterovirus 71 —contrasted-with→ poliovirus
span.quote: Other enteroviruses, notably poliovirus, have remained antigenically stable for many years.

span.label: cryptic —part-of→ subgenogroup
span.quote: Genealogical analysis revealed that diverse lineages of genogroup B and C (subgenogroups B1 to B5 and C1 to C5) have each circulated cryptically in the human population for up to 5 years before causing large HFMD outbreaks, indicating the quiescent persistence of EV-71 in human populations.

span.label: immunogenic —part-of→ VP1
span.quote: The VP1 protein is highly exposed and usually targeted by host neutralizing antibodies, predisposing the VP1 gene to constant immune selective pressure.

span.label: recombination —distinct-from→ VP1
span.quote: Additionally, rigorous recombination analysis showed a lack of recombination in the capsid-encoding VP1 region, consistent with previous analyses on human enterovirus species ( 73 ).

span.label: likelihood ratio test
span.quote: This lineage-specific codon model was estimated using maximum likelihood and was compared, using a likelihood ratio test (LRT) with one degree of freedom, to a null model that assumes a uniform dN / dS ratio across all branches.

span.label: Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo
span.quote: Rates of evolution, molecular clock phylogenies, divergence times, demographic histories, and other evolutionary parameters were jointly estimated from heterochronous VP1 gene sequences of genogroups B and C (with sampling date ranges of 32 and 26 years, respectively) using the Bayesian MCMC method implemented in BEAST, version 1.4.8 ( 24 ).

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: The trees are midpoint rooted, and significant bootstrap support values (≥80%; 1,000 bootstrap replicates) are indicated by asterisks at major nodes.

span.label: multiple-comparison correction (Bonferroni)
span.quote: Potential recombinant sequences were suggested when more than three methods showed significant support for recombination with a Bonferroni-corrected P value cutoff of 0.05.

span.label: coefficient of variation
span.quote: Our analyses also indicated substantial heterogeneity in evolutionary rates among viral lineages, with an estimated coefficient of variation of 0.44 (95% credible region [CR], 0.28 to 0.57) and 0.39 (95% CR, 0.25 to 0.53) for genogroups B and C, respectively.

span.label: posterior probability
span.quote: Posterior probabilities were calculated with a burn-in of 2 million states and checked for convergence using Tracer, version 1.4 ( 64 ).

span.label: confidence interval
span.quote: We estimated that the common ancestor of human EV-71 likely emerged around 1941 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1929 to 1952), subsequently diverging into three genogroups: B, C, and the now extinct genogroup A.

span.label: Bayes factor
span.quote: Marginal-likelihood analysis ( 77 ) showed that a demographic model of exponential growth fits the VP1 data set better than a model of constant population size (log 10 Bayes factor, 7.6).

span.label: maximum likelihood
span.quote: Maximum-likelihood analyses showed that the evolution of EV-71 is driven by strong purifying selection, with estimates of mean dN / dS values ranging from 0.029 to 0.075 for all subgenogroups (except B3, for which the mean dN / dS is significantly higher) (Table 2 ).

span.label: gamma-distributed among-site rate variation
span.quote: Analyses were independently performed using the Hasegawa-Kishino-Yano (HKY) ( 32 ) and general time-reversible (GTR) ( 68 ) nucleotide substitution models, with a gamma-distributed among-site rate variation with four rate categories (γ 4 ) ( 84 ).

span.label: dN/dS
span.quote: Selection pressure on the EV-71 VP1 gene was investigated by estimating the ratio of nonsynonymous substitutions to synonymous substitutions ( dN / dS ) using the codon-based phylogenetic method implemented in CODEML (distributed in the PAML, version 4, package).

span.label: likelihood ratio test
span.quote: This lineage-specific codon model was estimated using maximum likelihood and was compared, using a likelihood ratio test (LRT) with one degree of freedom, to a null model that assumes a uniform dN / dS ratio across all branches.

span.label: Bayes factor
span.quote: Marginal-likelihood analysis ( 77 ) showed that a demographic model of exponential growth fits the VP1 data set better than a model of constant population size (log 10 Bayes factor, 7.6).

span.label: Bonferroni correction
span.quote: Potential recombinant sequences were suggested when more than three methods showed significant support for recombination with a Bonferroni-corrected P value cutoff of 0.05.

span.label: credible interval
span.quote: with an estimated coefficient of variation of 0.44 (95% credible region [CR], 0.28 to 0.57) and 0.39 (95% CR, 0.25 to 0.53) for genogroups B and C, respectively

span.label: confidence interval
span.quote: We estimated that the common ancestor of human EV-71 likely emerged around 1941 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1929 to 1952), subsequently diverging into three genogroups: B, C, and the now extinct genogroup A.

span.label: coefficient of variation
span.quote: Our analyses also indicated substantial heterogeneity in evolutionary rates among viral lineages, with an estimated coefficient of variation of 0.44 (95% credible region [CR], 0.28 to 0.57) and 0.39 (95% CR, 0.25 to 0.53) for genogroups B and C, respectively.

span.label: posterior probability
span.quote: Posterior probabilities were calculated with a burn-in of 2 million states and checked for convergence using Tracer, version 1.4 ( 64 ).

span.label: maximum likelihood
span.quote: To chronologically trace the evolution of nonsynonymous changes throughout the evolutionary history of EV-71 subgenogroup C1 (i.e., 1986 to 2006), we reconstructed nonsynonymous changes from the heterochronous virus sequences using a joint maximum-likelihood method ( 59 ), as implemented in HyPhy, version 0.99 ( 58 ).

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: The trees are midpoint rooted, and significant bootstrap support values (≥80%; 1,000 bootstrap replicates) are indicated by asterisks at major nodes.

span.label: Markov chain Monte Carlo
span.quote: Phylogenetic estimates of EV-71 genogroups B and C and their respective subgenogroups were consistent among different phylogenetic approaches, specifically, maximum-likelihood (ML), neighbor-joining (using PAUP*, version 4.0 beta [ 78 ]) and the Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method (using BEAST [ 24 ], described below).

span.label: p-value
span.quote: revealed a significantly lower dN / dS ratio for the trunk lineages (0.030 ± 0.009) than for the terminal lineages (0.064 ± 0.008) ( P = 0.055)

span.label: The common ancestor of human enterovirus 71 is dated to about 1941, after which the virus split into genogroups B, C and the now-extinct genogroup A.
span.quote: We estimated that the common ancestor of human EV-71 likely emerged around 1941 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1929 to 1952), subsequently diverging into three genogroups: B, C, and the now extinct genogroup A.

span.label: Each subgenogroup of genogroups B and C circulated undetected in humans for up to five years before it caused a large hand, foot and mouth disease outbreak.
span.quote: Genealogical analysis revealed that diverse lineages of genogroup B and C (subgenogroups B1 to B5 and C1 to C5) have each circulated cryptically in the human population for up to 5 years before causing large HFMD outbreaks, indicating the quiescent persistence of EV-71 in human populations.

span.label: The VP1 gene evolves under strong purifying selection, with mean dN/dS between 0.029 and 0.075 in every subgenogroup except B3.
span.quote: Maximum-likelihood analyses showed that the evolution of EV-71 is driven by strong purifying selection, with estimates of mean dN / dS values ranging from 0.029 to 0.075 for all subgenogroups (except B3, for which the mean dN / dS is significantly higher) (Table 2 ).

span.label: In subgenogroup C1 the trunk lineages have a lower dN/dS (0.030) than the terminal lineages (0.064), the opposite of the pattern expected under antigenic-drift-style positive selection along the trunk.
span.quote: Lineage-specific codon-based analyses of subgenogroup C1 VP1 genes revealed a significantly lower dN / dS ratio for the trunk lineages (0.030 ± 0.009) than for the terminal lineages (0.064 ± 0.008) ( P = 0.055).

span.label: No homologous recombination was detectable in the capsid-encoding VP1 region, so the phylogenetic and dating analyses are not confounded by recombination.
span.quote: Additionally, rigorous recombination analysis showed a lack of recombination in the capsid-encoding VP1 region, consistent with previous analyses on human enterovirus species ( 73 ).

span.label: Rises in viral genetic diversity coincide with epidemic onsets and are driven partly by the appearance of new subgenogroups.
span.quote: In addition, rises in genetic diversity are correlated with the onset of epidemics, driven in part by the emergence of novel EV-71 subgenogroups.

span.label: VP1 codon 98 changed repeatedly and unidirectionally (glutamic acid to lysine or glycine) on terminal branches but never on trunk branches, so lineages that acquired the change did not persist.
span.quote: For instance, the VP1 position 98 underwent frequent amino acid replacements (e.g., E98K/G, n = 13; K98N, n = 1) on terminal lineages, but no changes at this site were found on the trunk lineages.

span.label: A demographic model of exponential population growth fits the VP1 data far better than a constant-population-size model.
span.quote: Marginal-likelihood analysis ( 77 ) showed that a demographic model of exponential growth fits the VP1 data set better than a model of constant population size (log 10 Bayes factor, 7.6).

span.label: Several trunk residues toggled back and forth over time: position 145 went glutamic acid to glutamine and back, 262 isoleucine to valine and back, and 289 alanine to threonine and back.
span.quote: For instance, glutamic acid at position 145 changed to glutamine in 1985 to 1986 and later reverted to glutamic acid in 1988 to 1989; isoleucine at position 262 was replaced by valine in 1990 to 1994 and returned to isoleucine in 1997 to 1999; alanine at position 289 changed to threonine in 1994 to 1996 and reverted to alanine in 1998 to 2005.

span.label: Subgenogroups B1 to B5, C1, C2 and C4 are globally distributed, whereas C3 is confined to Korea and C5 to Vietnam.
span.quote: Phylogeographic analysis revealed that subgenogroups B1 to B5, C1, C2, and C4 exhibit a global, cosmopolitan distribution, whereas the C3 and C5 lineages are restricted to Korea and Vietnam, respectively (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: The VP1 gene evolves at about 4.2 to 4.6 x 10^-3 substitutions per site per year, higher than earlier linear-regression estimates.
span.quote: The evolutionary rate of the VP1 gene was estimated to be 4.5 × 10 −3 to 4.6 × 10 −3 and 4.2 × 10 −3 substitutions/site/year for genogroups B and C, respectively (Table 1 ).

span.label: Choice of coalescent demographic model made no significant difference to the estimated divergence dates.
span.quote: The evolutionary models employed in the coalescent analyses had no significant effect on estimated dates (Table 1 ; see also Table S2 in the supplemental material, where divergence times obtained under two further models are provided).

span.label: the common ancestor of EV-71 dates to about 1941
span.quote: We estimated that the common ancestor of human EV-71 likely emerged around 1941 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1929 to 1952), subsequently diverging into three genogroups: B, C, and the now extinct genogroup A.

span.label: each subgenogroup circulated undetected for 1 to 5 years before its first outbreak
span.quote: Similar results were obtained for genogroup C lineages; the various subgenogroups within genogroup C were identified only 1 to 5 years after their dates of common ancestry (Table 1 ).

span.label: the same subgenogroup in different countries reflects separate lineages, not one strain travelling
span.quote: This also suggests that contemporary HFMD outbreaks in different countries caused by the same EV-71 subgenogroup may be the result of different lineages and are less likely to have been caused by the sequential transmission of a single lineage between countries ( 72 ).

span.label: VP1 evolves under strong purifying selection despite substitution rates comparable to influenza and HIV-1
span.quote: This strong signal of negative selection is perhaps surprising, given that estimates of EV-71 VP1 substitution rates are similar to those observed for the surface glycoproteins of the influenza virus ( 26 ) and HIV-1 ( 67 ), which show evidence of repeated positive selection.

span.label: trunk lineages carry a lower dN/dS than terminal lineages in subgenogroup C1
span.quote: Lineage-specific codon-based analyses of subgenogroup C1 VP1 genes revealed a significantly lower dN / dS ratio for the trunk lineages (0.030 ± 0.009) than for the terminal lineages (0.064 ± 0.008) ( P = 0.055).

span.label: position 98 changes repeatedly on terminal lineages and never on the trunk, and the changes are directional
span.quote: For instance, the VP1 position 98 underwent frequent amino acid replacements (e.g., E98K/G, n = 13; K98N, n = 1) on terminal lineages, but no changes at this site were found on the trunk lineages.

span.label: amino acids toggle - changing and reverting - on the core trunk over 3 to 5 year spans
span.quote: Moreover, most of this amino acid toggling occurred on the core trunk branches, and changed residues persisted for about 3 to 5 years (Fig. 4 ).

span.label: only 14 nonsynonymous substitutions occur on the trunk, at 10 sites
span.quote: Only 14 nonsynonymous substitutions are observed on the trunk branches, and they occur at 10 different sites.

span.label: no recombination was detectable in VP1
span.quote: Fortunately, we found no evidence of homologous recombination within our data sets, suggesting that our evolutionary analyses (which do not explicitly incorporate recombination) are unlikely to be strongly affected in this instance.

span.label: reconstructed diversity dynamics match four decades of independent surveillance data
span.quote: Crucially, the dynamics of the skyline plot are largely in agreement with the global surveillance data of laboratory-confirmed EV-71 cases (Fig. 3B ) longitudinally recorded over the past 4 decades ( 9 ), suggesting that elevation in genetic diversity is correlated with EV-71 epidemics, as has been previously observed for the human influenza A virus ( 65 ).

span.label: exponential growth fits the data better than constant population size
span.quote: Marginal-likelihood analysis ( 77 ) showed that a demographic model of exponential growth fits the VP1 data set better than a model of constant population size (log 10 Bayes factor, 7.6).

span.label: C3 and C5 are geographically restricted while the other subgenogroups are cosmopolitan
span.quote: Phylogeographic analysis revealed that subgenogroups B1 to B5, C1, C2, and C4 exhibit a global, cosmopolitan distribution, whereas the C3 and C5 lineages are restricted to Korea and Vietnam, respectively (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: outbreaks recur on a roughly 2 to 3 year cycle
span.quote: Intriguingly, EV-71 outbreaks do appear to show a cyclical pattern, occurring about every 2 to 3 years.

span.label: core trunk branches and terminal branches
